A true row (expected got = a resolving class) that the counter refuses is counted in refused_true; `accepted` counts only rows whose expectation is non-resolving. Columns: id, where (lane|fixture), rev (BASE = the r79 lane base; F0 = the r79 fixture commit; R1-R3 = fixture commits; R5 = R3 + R4 + r82 copies, the r81 R4 relabelled), population (r77|r78), item, class, target, expect (REFUSED|MISMATCH|<class>), expect_rc, source note.

r88 C1: the `_whole` BEFORE-byte half. The R11 declaration names the L06 token only as the suffix of `xtests/vault/.../.git` (the byte before it is a path character), so only a rule that checks the preceding byte refuses the row; a mutant that drops it resolves QUARANTINED.

r88 C1: the `_ledger` duplicate-id refusal. The harness appends a second P01 row to the frozen r77 ledger; the counter must print `LEDGER-REFUSED id=P01` and exit 1. A mutant that drops `r[0] in ledger` accepts the duplicate (last row wins) and the row goes red.

r89 C1: `_whole` examines every occurrence (S88MutCounter F4 kills m18d). R12 carries the token twice — first as a suffix, later whole — so only the full loop resolves it.
r89 C1: the `_ledger` duplicate-id refusal with a DIFFERENT target (S88MutCounter F2 kills m17b). Same row type as LD1, only the appended target differs (`census/nowhere/ld1b`).
r89 C1: the `_ledger` malformed-row guard `len(r) < 3` (S88MutCounter F3 kills m17c). The harness appends a 2-column row; pristine refuses it, the mutant raises IndexError.

r90 C1: the SAME malformed-row guard reached under an id ABSENT from the frozen r77 ledger. The appended row is `ZZ9<TAB>ABSENT` (2 columns); pristine refuses it on len(r)<3 and prints `LEDGER-REFUSED id=ZZ9`, while m17c (len guard dropped) writes ledger[ZZ9]=(r[1], r[2]) and raises IndexError with no marker. LD2 could not bind this guard because its id P02 is already in the ledger (r89 A1).

r91 C1: the `_ledger` duplicate-id refusal for an IDENTICAL duplicate (same class and target). A rule keyed on a class conflict (`ld1c`) or on a class-or-target conflict (`ld1d`) accepts it and prints no marker; pristine refuses on the duplicate id alone.

r91 C1: the malformed guard's ONE-COLUMN reach: the appended row is `ZY8` alone. Pristine refuses on len(r)<3; a reader spelling the guard `len(r)==2` stores r[1]/r[2] and crashes (IndexError, no marker).

r91 C1: the ledger WIDTH-ACCEPTANCE clause: with the frozen 4-column ledger unchanged, item P04 resolves MOVED only if a recorded 4-column entry is accepted; a reader that refuses every non-3-column row finds no entry and reports UNRESOLVED.

r91 C1: `_whole` examines occurrences left to right. R13 carries the token WHOLE first and as a suffix later; pristine resolves it, a reader that starts at `line.rfind` sees only the suffix and refuses.

r91 C1: the six PATHCH punctuation predecessors `. _ @ + ~ -`: R13 names the token after each in one line; pristine refuses (all six are path bytes), a PATHCH narrowed to alnum+`/` sees the first occurrence as whole and resolves.
